messages:
Maria: Quick sync — did a small bring-up for zeta11b on our chat eval set. Ran fp16 baseline, int8 and int6 quant runs. posting the short TL;DR and a suggested routing/rollout. wanted product/GTN input before we push flags.

Devin: Results snapshot:
- fp16 baseline: avg quality score 87.4, p95 latency 210ms, cost = $1.00 (norm)
- int8 (q4_0 style): quality 86.2 (-1.2 pts ~ -1.37%), p95 latency 230ms (+20ms), cost = $0.38 (~2.6x savings)
- int6 (aggressive pack): quality 85.0 (-2.4 pts ~ -2.75%), p95 latency 245ms (+35ms), cost = $0.26 (~3.85x savings)
Notes: most degradation shows up on long-form instruction completions and token-recall cases. throughput improved (tokens/sec) on steady-state for both quant variants, but int6 had slightly higher error variance.

Maria: quick ask for GTN/product: do we 1) default new low-cost route to int8 with fp16 fallback, 2) expose int6 behind an explicit "cheap" tier, or 3) keep fp16 default and use quant for dedicated routing only?

AJ: Product perspective — customers expect "no visible regressions" for chat by default. I'd prefer int8 on a labeled "eco" plan, not default. Can we make fallback automatic and transparent? also need dollar-per-1M-token numbers for pricing page.

Devin: dollar numbers: int8 = $380 per 1M tokens (baseline $1000), int6 = $260 per 1M tokens. these are rough after infra amortization. Also modeled tail-risk: worst-case quality regression spikes for int6 on certain prompt clusters (long-context summarization) — ~6% of traffic could see >3pt drop.

Nora: For GTN we need a recommended rollout plan and guardrails. Suggestion: Canary 5–10% for 48h, monitor eval set + production signal (user satis, retry rate). If quality regression >1.5% on eval or user retries +0.5pp, rollback.

Sam: SRE notes: int8 p95 latency bump is acceptable but put a latency guard: if p95 > 300ms for 5m window, route to fp16. Also enable autoscale buffer on quant nodes (burst capacity) to avoid queueing spikes.

quant-bot: automated eval summary (run 24640012):
- eval-set (10k prompts): fp16=87.4, int8=86.2 (-1.37%), int6=85.0 (-2.75%)
- regressions by category: factuality 0.8% int8, 1.9% int6; long-form coherence: 0.9% int8, 2.7% int6
- latency p50/p95 (ms): fp16 125/210, int8 130/230, int6 135/245

Maria: proposed rollout YAML (for ops/config) — small snippet:
```
routing_rules:
  - name: zeta11b_eco_canary
    percent: 10
    model_variant: zeta11b-int8
    fallback: zeta11b-fp16
    monitors: [eval_quality, prod_retry_rate, latency_p95]
    rollback_criteria:
      eval_quality_drop_pct: 1.5
      prod_retry_pp_increase: 0.5
      latency_p95_ms: 300
```

AJ: That looks good. For GTN pages we should call the tier "Eco (quantized)" and list expected cost savings ~60–70% with a small asterisk about edge-case regressions. Also add recommended prompt classifier/labeling for long-context workloads so we can keep those on fp16.

Devin: Operational notes: we should add two short eval suites to the rollout: 1) long-context summarization (1k prompts) and 2) factuality/QA (1k prompts). Run daily during canary and push alert if difference > 1.2 pts.

Nora: +1 on prompt classifier. GTN wants a feature flag to force fp16 for any route labeled "sensitive-doc" or "long-context".

Sam: will add the latency circuit-breaker and autoscale buffer. Also suggest storing KV-cache-compatible quant artifacts to avoid mismatch when falling back — else we pay large memory copy costs.

Maria: Final recommendation (for now):
- Enable zeta11b-int8 as an "Eco" route, 10% canary for 48h with the YAML guards above.
- Expose int6 as experimental/opt-in only for non-critical workloads (batch embedding or burst chat) behind an explicit flag.
- Add the two short eval suites + prod signal checks.
- GTN to mark "long-context" and "sensitive" as fp16 by default.

AJ: Approved for canary from product side. please include the pricing blurb + example numbers. :thumbsup:

Maria: I'll open the rollout PR and attach eval outputs. thanks everyone.

Devin: PR link when ready pls, will add quant ops playbook snippets.

Nora: we'll prepare GTN docs and the prompt classifier guidelines.

Sam: added to my oncall checklist. monitoring will be live for canary.

quant-bot: note: baseline drift check scheduled daily; will post summary to #eng-ml-canaries channel.
